title: Differentiability of the shape function in the planar corner growth model
common_notation: Let $e_1=(1,0)$, $e_2=(0,1)$ and $\ell(z)=z_1+z_2$. The order $u\le v$ means $u_i\le v_i$ for $i=1,2$. The site weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^2}$ are independent with common probability law $\mu$ on $\mathbb R$. Write $\mathbb P$ and $\mathbb E$ for probability and expectation.

For a real number $a$, write $a^+=\max\{a,0\}$ and $a^-=\max\{-a,0\}$. For $z=(z_1,z_2)$, $|z|_1=|z_1|+|z_2|$ and $|z|_\infty=\max\{|z_1|,|z_2|\}$. The indicator $\mathbf1\{E\}$ is $1$ when $E$ holds and $0$ otherwise.

A directed path $P=(x_0,\ldots,x_k)$ has increments $x_{i+1}-x_i\in\{e_1,e_2\}$, length $|P|=k$ and weight $W(P)=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\omega_{x_i}$. Thus the first vertex is included and the last is excluded. For $u\le v$, $L_{u,v}=\max_{P:u\to v}W(P)$.

The shape $g:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^2\to[-\infty,\infty]$ is defined by $g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for every fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^2$, when these deterministic limits exist. Rounding is coordinatewise. The hypotheses of each result determine existence and finiteness. Uniform convergence and the other shape properties are proved separately. Write $\mathcal U=\{(t,1-t):0\le t\le1\}$.
notes: Section 6 first proves the bounded-weight case. The full theorem under the stated moment assumptions uses Appendix B.
Lemma B.2 supplies the general-weight proof of Lemma 3.2. Remark 5.8 changes the endpoints and intervals in the general-weight version of Lemma 5.7.

results.label: Theorem 2.1
results.title: The shape is differentiable
results.summary: The directional limit shape $g$ has a derivative at every point of the open quadrant, assuming a negative moment of order greater than one and a positive moment of order greater than four. The weight law may have atoms and the weights may take both signs.
definitions: The site weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^2}$ are independent with common probability law $\mu$ on $\mathbb R$. They are not almost surely constant. Put $\omega_z^+=\max\{\omega_z,0\}$ and $\omega_z^-=\max\{-\omega_z,0\}$.
For $u\le v$ coordinatewise, $L_{u,v}$ is the maximum of $\sum_{i=m}^{l-1}\omega_{x_i}$ over paths from $u=x_m$ to $v=x_l$ whose steps are $e_1$ or $e_2$.

The shape is defined by $g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for every fixed $x\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^2$. The assumptions below ensure that these deterministic limits exist and are finite. The event of probability one in this definition may depend on $x$.
Differentiability at $x$ means that there is a vector $v_x\in\mathbb R^2$ for which $g(x+h)-g(x)-v_x\cdot h=o(\|h\|_2)$ as $h\to0$. The vector $v_x$ is the gradient $\nabla g(x)$.
results.statement: If there are $p_->1$ and $p_+>4$ such that $\mathbb E[(\omega_0^-)^{p_-}]<\infty$ and $\mathbb E[(\omega_0^+)^{p_+}]<\infty$, then $g$ is differentiable at every $x\in\mathbb R_{>0}^2$. Equivalently, it is differentiable at every $\xi=(t,1-t)$ with $0<t<1$.

coverage.scope: The full differentiability theorem is certified. The certificate also includes existence and uniqueness of the directional shape, together with the regularity and uniform convergence proved earlier in the paper.

results.label: Theorem 2.2
results.title: Where the shape equals the largest weight
results.summary: If the weights have a finite largest possible value $M$, the theorem identifies exactly the directions where $g$ equals $M$. It also proves differentiability at the endpoints of this set.
definitions: The site weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^2}$ are independent with common law $\mu$. An up-right path has steps $e_1=(1,0)$ or $e_2=(0,1)$, and its weight is $W(x_{m:n})=\sum_{i=m}^{n-1}\omega_{x_i}$, so its last vertex is not collected. The directional shape is $g(z)=\lim_{n\to\infty}L_{0,\lfloor nz\rfloor}/n$ almost surely for each fixed $z\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^2$; $L_{u,v}$ is the largest path weight from $u$ to $v$.

The paper assumes that $\mu$ is not concentrated at one point, $\mathbb E[(\omega_0^-)^{p_-}]<\infty$ for some $p_->1$, and $\mathbb E[(\omega_0^+)^{p_+}]<\infty$ for some $p_+>4$, where $t^-=\max(-t,0)$ and $t^+=\max(t,0)$. These assumptions give a finite, continuous, concave shape $g$ with $g(cz)=cg(z)$ for $c\ge0$ and a uniform shape theorem.

Let $M=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:\mu(( -\infty,t])=1\}$, with $\inf\varnothing=\infty$ and put $\omega^{\rm top}_z=\mathbf1\{\omega_z=M\}$ when $M<\infty$; if $M=\infty$, set these indicators to zero. Let $g_{\rm top}$ be the directional shape for these indicator weights, $\mathcal U=\{(t,1-t):0\le t\le1\}$, and $\mathcal U_{\rm top}=\{\zeta\in\mathcal U:g_{\rm top}(\zeta)=1\}$.

Set $p=\mu(\{M\})$. For independent site variables taking value one with probability $q$ and zero with probability $1-q$, let $R_n$ be the set of points $z\in\mathbb Z^2_{\ge0}$ with $z_1+z_2=n$ that can be reached from the origin by an up-right path whose site variables are all one. Define $p_c=\inf\{q\in[0,1]:\mathbb P_q(R_n\ne\varnothing\text{ for every }n)>0\}$. For $p>p_c$, $\beta_p=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\max\{z_1:z\in R_n\}$ on the event that all $R_n$ are nonempty, under the probability law $\mathbb P_p$. This limit is deterministic and lies in $(1/2,1)$.

The uniform approximation used by the proof means that, almost surely, for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $N<\infty$ with $|L_{0,z}-g(z)|\le\varepsilon|z|_1$ for all $z\in\mathbb Z^2_{\ge0}$ with $|z|_1\ge N$, where $|z|_1=|z_1|+|z_2|$. It is a proved property of the shape, not part of its directional definition.
results.statement: Assume $M<\infty$. Then $\mathcal U_{\rm top}=\{\zeta\in\mathcal U:g(\zeta)=M\}$ and $g(\zeta)<M$ for $\zeta\in\mathcal U\setminus\mathcal U_{\rm top}$. If $p<p_c$, this set is empty. If $p=p_c$, it is $\{(1/2,1/2)\}$ and $g$ is differentiable there. If $p>p_c$, it is $\{(t,1-t):1-\beta_p\le t\le\beta_p\}$ and $g$ is differentiable at both endpoints.

coverage.scope: The released proofs establish differentiability at directions with $g_{\rm top}(\zeta)=1$. The linked interval description does not include the printed classification into $p<p_c$, $p=p_c$ and $p>p_c$. Those cases are therefore not marked as fully certified here.

results.label: Lemma 2.3
results.title: Two linear bounds for the shape
results.summary: The linear functions obtained from the left and right derivatives of $g$ bound $g$ from above. Each agrees with $g$ at $\xi$ and approximates it to first order on its own side.
definitions: The site weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^2}$ are independent with common law $\mu$. An up-right path has steps $e_1=(1,0)$ or $e_2=(0,1)$, and its weight is $W(x_{m:n})=\sum_{i=m}^{n-1}\omega_{x_i}$, so its last vertex is not collected. For this deterministic statement, $g:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^2\to\mathbb R$, is finite and continuous. It is positively homogeneous, meaning $g(cz)=cg(z)$ for $c\ge0$, and concave, meaning $g(tx+(1-t)y)\ge tg(x)+(1-t)g(y)$ for $x,y\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^2$ and $0\le t\le1$.

Fix $\xi=(\xi_1,1-\xi_1)$ with $0<\xi_1<1$. Write $\ell(z)=z_1+z_2$, $r(z)=(1-\xi_1)z_1-\xi_1z_2$, $e=(1,-1)$, and $\theta_0=\min(\xi_1,1-\xi_1)$. Thus $z=\ell(z)\xi+r(z)e$; $r(z)$ measures the displacement from the line in direction $\xi$ on the same level $\ell(z)$.
Set $\varphi(t)=g(\xi+te)$, $a_-=\varphi'(0-)$ and $a_+=\varphi'(0+)$, the left and right derivatives of this concave function. Define $f_\pm(z)=g(\xi)\ell(z)+a_\pm r(z)$ and $f=(f_-+f_+)/2$.
The notation $q(h)=o(|h|)$ means $q(h)/|h|\to0$ in the stated limit.
results.statement: For every $z\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^2$, $f_-(z)\ge g(z)$ and $f_+(z)\ge g(z)$, while $f_-(\xi)=f_+(\xi)=f(\xi)=g(\xi)$. Moreover, $f_-(\xi+he)-g(\xi+he)=o(|h|)$ as $h\uparrow0$, and $f_+(\xi+he)-g(\xi+he)=o(|h|)$ as $h\downarrow0$.

coverage.scope: Both displayed inequalities, the equalities at $\xi$, and both one-sided limits are certified. This part of the proof uses only the stated properties of the deterministic function $g$, rather than additional assumptions about random weights.

results.label: Lemma 3.1
results.title: High-weight paths near a prescribed segment
results.summary: For any fixed pair of endpoints satisfying the displayed direction and distance bounds, a path can usually stay near the straight segment between them while collecting almost the shape-predicted weight. The probability bound works for every such pair.

coverage.scope: The complete statement for all endpoint pairs on the same event is certified, including unbounded weights. Lemma B.2 supplies the paper's proof under the general weight assumptions.

results.label: Proposition 3.4
results.title: Paths rarely exceed either linear bound
results.summary: In a strip whose length is much greater than its width, it is unlikely that any path collects more than a supporting linear function predicts, by a fixed multiple of the width.

For $s>0$, $R>0$ and a positive integer $n$, the strip is $\{z\in\mathbb Z^2:0\le\ell(z)\le n,\ |r(z)|\le Rs\}$. A path crossing it has one vertex on each level $0,\ldots,n$; its starting point need not be the origin.

coverage.scope: The conclusion is certified for each of the two functions $f_-$ and $f_+$ and every $R>0$. The released estimate gives a bound uniform over all sufficiently large ratios $n/s$, which implies the displayed sequential limit.

results.label: Lemma 4.1
results.title: Raising finitely many weights at small probability cost
results.summary: Independently at each chosen site, replace the weight by the larger of itself and a fresh sample with a small probability $\delta$. The new law has a controlled density relative to the old law, and most weights below the largest possible value have a definite chance to increase by a definite amount.
definitions: The site weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^2}$ are independent with common law $\mu$. An up-right path has steps $e_1=(1,0)$ or $e_2=(0,1)$, and its weight is $W(x_{m:n})=\sum_{i=m}^{n-1}\omega_{x_i}$, so its last vertex is not collected. The directional shape is $g(z)=\lim_{n\to\infty}L_{0,\lfloor nz\rfloor}/n$ almost surely for each fixed $z\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^2$; $L_{u,v}$ is the largest path weight from $u$ to $v$.

Let $\mathcal R\subset\mathbb Z^2$ be finite and $0<\delta<1$. Let $(\widetilde\omega_z)$ be an independent copy of the weights and $(\chi_z)$ independent variables with $\mathbb Q(\chi_z=1)=\delta$ and $\mathbb Q(\chi_z=0)=1-\delta$, independent of both weight collections. Put $\omega'_z=\max(\omega_z,\widetilde\omega_z)$ if $z\in\mathcal R$ and $\chi_z=1$, and put $\omega'_z=\omega_z$ otherwise. Write $\mathbb P'$ for the law of $\omega'$ and $\mathbb Q$ for the joint law of $\omega,\widetilde\omega,\chi$.

Let $F(t)=\mu(( -\infty,t])$, $F^{-1}(q)=\inf\{t:F(t)\ge q\}$ for $0<q<1$, and $M=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:F(t)=1\}$, with $\inf\varnothing=\infty$. A density $D=d\mathbb P'/d\mathbb P$ means that $\mathbb P'(A)=\mathbb E[D\mathbf1_A]$ for every measurable environment event $A$. If $M=\infty$, the set $\{M\}$ in the formula below is interpreted as empty.
results.statement: The modified weights satisfy $\omega'_z\ge\omega_z$, their law $\mathbb P'$ is a product law, and a density $D$ exists with $\mathbb E[D^2]\le\exp(3\delta^2|\mathcal R|)$. For $0<\alpha<1$ and $F(t)\le1-\alpha$, define $\psi_\alpha(t)=F^{-1}(F(t)+\alpha/2)-t$. Then $\psi_\alpha(t)>0$. For every $\beta>0$ there are $0<\alpha<1/2$ and $c'>0$ for which $I=\{t<M:F(t)\le1-\alpha,\ \psi_\alpha(t)\ge c'\}$ satisfies $\mu(\mathbb R\setminus(I\cup\{M\}))\le\beta$. Given the original weights, each $z\in\mathcal R$ with $\omega_z\in I$ has conditional probability at least $\delta\alpha/2$ of satisfying $\omega'_z\ge\omega_z+c'$, and these increase events are conditionally independent across sites.

coverage.scope: All the displayed assertions are certified across the linked declarations, including the density bound, positivity of $\psi_\alpha$, the common set $I$, and the conditional probability and independence statements.

results.label: Lemma A.1
results.title: An infinite up-right path through likely events
results.summary: If events fail with sufficiently small probability and events at sufficiently separated lattice sites are independent, then with positive probability an infinite up-right path from the origin visits only sites where the events occur.
definitions: The events $(G_v)_{v\in\mathbb Z^2_{\ge0}}$ are defined on a probability space. Write $\|v-w\|_\infty=\max(|v_1-w_1|,|v_2-w_2|)$. For a fixed integer $\kappa\ge0$, the required independence means that $G_{v_1},\ldots,G_{v_m}$ are independent whenever all distinct pairs satisfy $\|v_i-v_j\|_\infty>\kappa$. An up-right path has increments $(1,0)$ or $(0,1)$.
results.statement: For every integer $\kappa\ge0$ there is $\zeta(\kappa)>0$ such that the following holds. If the stated independence condition holds and $\mathbb P(G_v^c)\le\zeta(\kappa)$ for every $v\in\mathbb Z^2_{\ge0}$, then $\mathbb P\{\exists(v_i)_{i\ge0}:v_0=(0,0),\ v_{i+1}-v_i\in\{(1,0),(0,1)\},\ G_{v_i}\text{ occurs for every }i\}\,>0$.

coverage.scope: The full statement is certified, for every probability space and every event family meeting the displayed conditions. The required path starts at the origin, so the event $G_0$ is included.

results.label: Lemma B.1
results.title: A lower bound for selected path weights
results.summary: Choose paths after observing only the set $V_T=\{z:\omega_z<-T\}$, and require the paths to avoid collecting vertices of $V_T$. The lemma gives an explicit upper bound for the probability that any selected path has a very negative total weight.
definitions: The site weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^2}$ are independent with common law $\mu$. Put $\omega_0^-=\max\{-\omega_0,0\}$. An admissible path takes steps $e_1=(1,0)$ or $e_2=(0,1)$; its weight is $W(x_{m:n})=\sum_{i=m}^{n-1}\omega_{x_i}$, so the final vertex is excluded. The last-passage time $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of an up-right path from $u$ to $v$.

The shape $g$ is defined by $g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^2=\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^2$. The appendix uses the proved shape theorem: $g$ is finite, continuous, homogeneous of degree one and concave, and, almost surely, $\sup_{z\in\mathbb Z^2_{\ge0},\,|z|_1\ge R}|L_{0,z}-g(z)|/|z|_1\to0$ as $R\to\infty$. These are proved properties, not additional parts of the definition of $g$.
Assume $\mathbb E[(\omega_0^-)^{p_-}]<\infty$ for some $p_->1$. Write $C_-=\mathbb E\omega_0^-$ and $C_{p_-}=\mathbb E[(\omega_0^-)^{p_-}]$.

For $T>0$ let $V_T=\{z\in\mathbb Z^2:\omega_z<-T\}$ and $\mathcal F_T=\sigma(\mathbf1_{\{\omega_z<-T\}}:z\in\mathbb Z^2)$. A family chosen using only $V_T$ means that the family is measurable with respect to $\mathcal F_T$. Its choice cannot use the actual weight values beyond those indicators.

For a path $\alpha=(x_0,\ldots,x_q)$, its length is $|\alpha|=q$ and its collected vertices are $x_0,\ldots,x_{q-1}$. The integers $N,n\ge0$ bound the number of selected paths and their lengths. The integer $K\ge1$ and real numbers $b,t>0$ are free parameters in the probability bound.
results.statement: Let $T>0$ satisfy $\mu([-T,\infty))\ge1/2$. results.notes: The source states its standing shape assumptions by citing Theorem 5.1 and Remark 5.1(ii) of Limiting shape for directed percolation models. The definition above keeps directional limits separate from the proved uniform approximation.

coverage.scope: The displayed bound is certified when every selected path lies in one fixed, deterministic finite set of lattice sites. The paper's statement does not require such a containing set. Paths may still be chosen by observing the full set $V_T$.

results.label: Lemma B.2
results.title: Paths joining every pair of endpoints

coverage.scope: The release constructs one suitable set $\mathcal N$ and proves the forward and backward path bounds for that set at all sufficiently large scales. It does not provide the paper's assertion for every prescribed set $\mathcal N$ satisfying the spacing conditions.

results.label: Lemma B.5
results.title: Paths can go around the very negative vertices
results.summary: With probability tending to one, vertices that obstruct paths avoiding $\omega_z<-T_k$ occur only in small groups. This lets the proof follow a line with a uniformly bounded sideways displacement, reach suitable endpoints, and remove only a bounded number of endpoint vertices.
definitions: Fix an interior direction $\xi=(\xi_1,1-\xi_1)$ with $0<\xi_1<1$. Put $\ell(z)=z_1+z_2$, $r(z)=z_1-\xi_1\ell(z)$ and $\theta_0=\min\{\xi_1,1-\xi_1\}$. Thus $z=\ell(z)\xi+r(z)(e_1-e_2)$. The coordinate $r$ measures displacement from the line in direction $\xi$ on each level $\ell=I$.
For a directed path $\pi=(x_m,\ldots,x_n)$, with $\ell(x_i)=i$ and increments $e_1$ or $e_2$, write $W(\pi)=\sum_{i=m}^{n-1}\omega_{x_i}$. Its length is $|\pi|=n-m$; the last vertex is not collected.

Fix $A,R,\varepsilon_0>0$. Put $s_k=2^k$, let $\Lambda_k=2^{m_k}\le s_k^3$ be the lengths used in Section 5, and put $t_k=\varepsilon_0s_k/k$ for fixed $\varepsilon_0>0$. Only these size bounds are needed in this estimate; no new crossing-probability assumption is imposed.
The fixed constant $C_*=50/\theta_0$ controls the allowed lengths of the connecting paths.
Let $p'>1$ satisfy $\mathbb E[(\omega_0^-)^{p'}]<\infty$ and put $C_-=\mathbb E[\omega_0^-]$. Fix $q\ge1$ and integers $m_1,K_1,K_2\ge1$ with $m_1p'>40$, $(K_1+1)p'>4$ and $K_2(p'-1)>2q+2$.

The threshold is $T_k=t_k/(4K_2)$. Put $V_k=\{z:\omega_z<-T_k\}$ and $\mathcal F_{V_k}=\sigma(\mathbf1\{z\in V_k\}:z\in\mathbb Z^2)$. A path chosen using only $\mathcal F_{V_k}$ may depend on which weights fall below $-T_k$, but not on their actual values. It avoids $V_k$ when none of its collected vertices belongs to $V_k$.

The finite region is $Q_k=\{z\in\mathbb Z^2:|\ell(z)|\le(A+5)\Lambda_k,\ |r(z)|\le(R+2C_1+10)s_k\}$. Here $C_1$ is a fixed constant in the path bounds of Lemma 5.7. Its size satisfies $|Q_k|\le C_{A,R}s_k^4$ for a constant independent of $k$.

For a lattice point $z$, let $A_k(z)$ be all endpoints reachable from $z$ by directed paths whose collected vertices avoid $V_k$, including $z$ itself. Let $A_k^{\leftarrow}(z)$ be all starting points from which such a path can end at $z$. Write $\overline V_k=\{z:|A_k(z)|<\infty\}$ and $\overline V_k^{\leftarrow}=\{z:|A_k^{\leftarrow}(z)|<\infty\}$. These finite-reachability sets are the paper's forward and backward trapped sets.

The path $\gamma^u$ through $u$ follows the line $r=r(u)$ and avoids $V_k$. At each forward step it prefers the successor whose $r$ coordinate is closer to that line and uses the other successor if the preferred one lies in $\overline V_k$. The backward rule uses predecessors and avoids $V_k\cup\overline V_k^{\leftarrow}$. The forward part is defined when $u\notin\overline V_k$, and the backward part when $u\notin V_k\cup\overline V_k^{\leftarrow}$; each part is run only while it stays in $Q_k$. The notation $\gamma^u(I)$ means its vertex at level $I$, when that part exists. For a nonparallel target line, the same rule compares each candidate's $r$ coordinate with the target line's $r$ coordinate on the next (or preceding) level.

Put $\theta_1=\theta_0/5$, $N_{\rm tr}=K_1(2m_1^2+1)^2$, $W_0=N_{\rm tr}+1$, $L=\lceil4(W_0+2)/\theta_1\rceil$, $r_0=K_1(2L+1)+N_{\rm tr}$, $D_1=2W_0/\theta_1+4W_0+2r_0+2L+8$ and $d_0=D_1+2m_1^2$. These constants are independent of $k$.

For $c>0$, $Q_k^{(c)}=\{z:\inf_{y\in Q_k}|z-y|_1\le c\}$. Let $c_0=W_0+2L+1$, $Q_k^+=Q_k^{(c_0)}$ and $Q_k^{++}=Q_k^{(c_0+m_1^2)}$. A cluster of $V_k\cap Q_k^{++}$ is a connected component when two vertices are joined if their $\ell^1$ distance is at most $d_0$.

Let $E_{\rm geo}$ be the event that each such cluster has at most $K_1$ vertices, and for every $z\in Q_k^+$ each set $A_k(z)$ and $A_k^{\leftarrow}(z)$ is either infinite or has fewer than $m_1^2$ elements. A forward trapped component is a component of $\overline V_k\cap Q_k^+$ when vertices at $\ell^1$ distance at most $D_1$ are joined. results.label: Remark B.4
results.title: Why this proof needs a moment above one
results.summary: This remark explains the assumption $\mathbb E[(\omega_0^-)^{p_-}]<\infty$ with $p_->1$. It also suggests a weaker logarithmic-moment condition, but does not prove a result under that condition.
definitions: Here $\omega_0^-=\max\{-\omega_0,0\}$. In the attachment construction, $s$ is the large scale, $m=\lceil\kappa s\rceil$ is the length of a short joining path, and $T=\eta s/(64K)$ is the threshold used to avoid vertices with $\omega_z<-T$. The constants $\kappa,\eta>0$ and integer $K\ge1$ are chosen in the proof. Write $p_T=\mathbb P(\omega_0<-T)$. The last-passage time $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of an up-right path from $u$ to $v$.

There are at most a constant times $s$ possible starting points. To make the probability of failure at any starting point tend to zero by addition of the individual failure bounds, the failure probability for one starting point must be $o(1/s)$. This notation means that $s$ times that probability tends to zero.
results.statement: The proof bounds a starting point's failure probability by a constant times $(mp_T)^K$. If a moment of order $p_->1$ is finite and $T$ is proportional to $s$, then $mp_T$ is bounded by a constant times $s^{1-p_-}$, so a fixed sufficiently large $K$ makes this bound $o(1/s)$. results.notes: Do not label the suggested logarithmic-moment condition as a proved theorem or as an assumption needed by the certified main theorem.

coverage.scope: This is an explanation of the proof and a proposed weakening of its assumptions. No certificate for the proposed logarithmic-moment result is identified here.

results.label: Appendix C.1
results.title: A law with no finite uniform shape limit
results.summary: A finite negative moment of order $p<1$ alone cannot guarantee a finite uniform shape theorem. This example has that moment, but along infinitely many interior endpoints the normalized last-passage time is arbitrarily negative.
definitions: Fix $0<p<1$ and choose $\alpha$ with $\max\{p,1/2\}<\alpha<1$. Let the independent site weights be nonpositive with $\mathbb P\{\omega_0<-t\}=(1+t)^{-\alpha}$ for $t\ge0$.
Put $\omega_0^-=\max\{-\omega_0,0\}$. For an endpoint $x$, $L_{0,x}$ is the maximum up-right path weight with the terminal vertex excluded. Write $|x|_1=|x_1|+|x_2|$.
The endpoint set is $\mathcal V=\{(3i,3j):i,j\ge1,\ 1/2\le i/j\le2\}$. It stays inside a cone separated from both axes, so the example concerns interior directions rather than behavior on an axis.
results.statement: For this law, $\mathbb E[(\omega_0^-)^p]<\infty$, $\mathbb E\omega_0^-=\infty$, and $\liminf_{x\in\mathcal V,\ |x|_1\to\infty}L_{0,x}/|x|_1=-\infty$ almost surely. This construction disproves sufficiency of a negative $p$-th moment with $p<1$; it does not by itself prove that every law with infinite negative first moment lacks a finite shape theorem.

coverage.scope: The constructed law, its two moment assertions and the almost-sure limit inferior along the specified set of endpoints are certified for each $0<p<1$.
